evidence.source: 漢語多功能字庫, Chinese University of Hong Kong
evidence.field: 構形初義; 甲骨文用例; 金文用例
evidence.text: The database records two competing origin analyses: three dots representing smallness, attributed to Shang Chengzuo and Yu Xingwu; or 小 as an early graph of 沙 depicting fine sand, attributed to Ma Xulun. It says 小 and 少 were one graph before differentiation. It cites oracle-bone 小雨 (《粹》1004), 小食 for afternoon, 小采 for dusk, bronze 小鼎, and 小子/小臣 for young nobles or lower officials. It gives no absolute dates for the cited artifacts or semantic developments.
evidence.title: 漢語多功能字庫：漢字甲骨部件分析—小

evidence.text: The page labels oracle-bone, bronze, small-seal and Shuowen stages. It asserts that the earlier marks depict scattered fine sand grains and says the middle dot in small-seal changed into a vertical stroke separating the other two. This is one source's analysis; the marks do not independently identify sand.
evidence.title: 漢字「小」：字形演變

evidence.text: The inspected File page identifies 小-seal.svg as a modern vector depiction of 小 in Shuowen seal-script style and links its original image. The page states public-domain dedication for the representation, alongside CC0 information. This is a modern redraw, not an ancient artifact photograph.
evidence.title: File:小-seal.svg

evidence.text: The inspected rights notice reserves intellectual property in the site's content and limits use absent a separate agreement; it does not provide CC0 reuse terms. Accordingly, its page is used as linked evidence, not as an image asset.
evidence.title: 智財權聲明

evidence.text: The required individual record endpoint for 小 could not be opened in this run (internal fetch error). The supplied local Unihan row records kMandarin xiǎo, but is local data and is not independently verified here as a character-specific external record.
evidence.title: Unihan Database Lookup

evidence.text: Supplied exact local rows: 小 xiǎo; 少 shǎo; 雀 què. These are current Mandarin metadata only, not evidence of ancient phonetic relationships. Their official individual Unihan click-through records for 小, 少, and 雀 were not verified as accessible in this run.
evidence.title: Unihan individual character lookup (endpoint unavailable)

evidence.text: Exact supplied rows: 小 xiǎo, MC sjewX, OC *[s]ewʔ (‘small’); 少 shǎo MC syewX OC *[s.t]ewʔ (‘few’) and shào MC syewH OC *[s-t]ewʔ-s (‘young’); 雀 què MC tsjak OC *[ts]ewk (‘sparrow’). These are Baxter–Sagart 2014 table notations, checked as local rows. The *[s]ewʔ and *[ts]ewk forms do not support an obvious rhyme match for a proposed 小→雀 sound role in that system; CUHK's component-role assertion can be reported as source-attributed, without treating the local forms as proof of a sound change.
evidence.title: BaxterSagartOCbyRadStr2014-09-20 (version 1.1)

search_audit.query: 小 oracle bone bronze character formation three dots sand grains 說文 字形演變
search_audit.outcome: Inspected CUHK and Academia Sinica character-specific pages, plus the exact Commons file page. CUHK reports rival accounts of the dots and early usages; Academia Sinica supports its own sand-grain account and description of the seal-form change. Commons identifies the selected seal glyph as a modern redraw with reuse information.

search_audit.query: site:humanum.arts.cuhk.edu.hk/Lexis/lexi-mf 小 甲骨文 小雨 小 少
search_audit.outcome: Opened page and inspected relevant lines describing disputed formation, early examples, and 小–少 relation.
Exact Commons file page opened. Verified graph identity, original-file link, modern redraw status and rights statement.

search_audit.query: Academia Sinica Xiaoxuetang 小 字形演變 小學堂 glyph CC0 image; site:unicode.org/cgi-bin/GetUnihanData.pl?codepoint=5C0F
search_audit.outcome: Xiaoxuetang landing page and Character Database rights notice inspected; no 小-specific Xiaoxuetang glyph record was retrieved. The Unicode per-character endpoint returned an internal fetch error.

gaps: Whether the earliest dots depict grains of sand or are abstract marks for smallness remains disputed. No inspected evidence establishes the specific depicted object or a phonetic borrowing of 沙; the sand analysis is attributed to Ma Xulun, not demonstrated as a sound loan.

CUHK reports an oracle-bone usage 小雨 with the citation 《粹》1004, but this research did not inspect a facsimile or establish the artifact's absolute date. It reports time expressions and later bronze uses without dates or a demonstrated semantic bridge from ‘small.’
The 小–少 shared-graph and differentiation account is reported by CUHK, but the lexical and graphic details are not settled by the material inspected here.

CUHK reports 小 as a sound component in 雀. Local Baxter–Sagart rows are included for both graphs, but do not by themselves explain that source-attributed phonetic role; the individual character pages and a phonetic-history account were not independently verified.
The official Unicode individual-record endpoint for 小 returned an internal fetch error. Local reading rows are identified as local provenance, not externally confirmed records.

No Xiaoxuetang single-character form page or image was obtained in the inspected pages. The selected image is therefore the Commons modern seal-script redraw, not an ancient artifact image. The separate Sinica Character Database page states All Rights Reserved, so no image from that site is proposed.

items.period: Modern vector redraw of the Shuowen small-seal form; depicts an ancient script style, not a dated artifact
items.tradition: Small seal script (小篆), Shuowen style
items.caption: A modern redraw of 小 in Shuowen seal-script style. The character database describes the middle mark as lengthening into a vertical stroke; this image illustrates the later form, not the disputed identity of the earlier marks.
items.alt: Modern vector drawing of 小 in seal-script style, with a central vertical stroke between two side strokes.
items.selection_reason: The exact Commons page identifies this image as the Shuowen seal-script form, provides the original image link, and documents reuse rights. It illustrates the later graphic stage discussed by the sources.
items.rights: Public-domain dedication for the modern vector representation; Commons page also records CC0 information.

limitations.text: This is a modern vector redraw of a historical script form, not a photograph or facsimile of an ancient inscription. No verified direct image candidate for an oracle-bone or bronze artifact was obtained.
